description: We are a team with a background in AI/ML, data analysis, and physics, building software for NASA’s astronaut health monitoring challenge. Our tool tracks health data over time, flags early warning signs, and predicts how key metrics may change on long missions, all through a clear, easy-to-read dashboard. Join us now and help us build something exciting!
summary:
CytoZoe is a local-first astronaut health evidence and review workspace. It imports two real NASA datasets: blood chemistry from the four Inspiration4 crew members (OSD-575) and a day of ISS radiation readings (DosTel1). It compares each person’s biomarkers with their own preflight baseline and the laboratory ranges supplied in the source. It also replays the radiation record separately, quarantining conflicting source rows instead of averaging them. Every finding links to its exact source row and a verified explanation built from fixed templates, with no AI model at runtime. Reviewers can save versioned follow-up notes with an audit trail and export a printable HTML and JSON handoff packet, all offline.

This addresses the challenge of health monitoring software for astronauts. On deep-space missions, Earth may be delayed or unreachable, so crews need to review health data independently. A spreadsheet can’t show what changed, where the uncertainty lies, or what was decided. CytoZoe closes that gap in one loop: inspect, explain, record, reopen, export. It is a research demonstration, not a clinical device, and it is transparent and traceable by design.
details:
CytoZoe runs entirely on a local machine: a React and TypeScript interface talks to a FastAPI backend and a SQLite database, with Recharts for charts and pandas for data handling. No cloud services or AI models are used at runtime. Three deterministic engines handle data validation, personal-baseline comparisons and radiation estimates, so every result can be traced and reproduced. We chose to replay real recorded NASA data instead of simulating live feeds, and to show data-quality problems openly. We also kept the health and radiation datasets separate, and made clear that this is a research demonstration and not a clinical tool.
Full details are in the attached document and video demo.
